question: At the unchanged selected first public record and physical error, do the predeclared baseline and six-edge-loop-toggled public corrections yield different complete second charge records when their public flux is identical?
role: Exact finite ideal charge-specific total-action contrast, not information gain, matched logical risk, policy-emitted JIT action or noisy schedule evaluation
source_basis: Jing Appendix A ideal red-X/projector rules as previously translated and tested
J6L/J6M periodic topology and anyon-free vacuum orbit
J7K predeclared homologically trivial equal-flux loop and five-site marginal censor

model.geometry_and_state: Paper-normalized periodic L=2 topology and the same J6M anyon-free positive-phase orbit; this is one ideal finite sector, not a general density channel
model.physical_error_and_first_record: Private physical red-X edges [0,4,3], complete signal-only first public binary charge/flux/vacuum record with bits [1,1] at variable sites [1,2], exact selected-record mass 1/4; fixed independently of the two subsequent actions
model.interventions: Relation-free public red-X corrections [0] and [1,30,32,34,35], fixed by J7K before five-site outcomes were known. The action difference is the already verified trivial six-edge cycle; both actions have identical public correction/second flux. No decoder policy is claimed to emit the long correction.
model.public_private_boundary: Only first/second full 24-site charge/flux/vacuum binary records and the declared correction are public. Orbit state, physical red-X error, residual supports and exact projector internals remain private generation/scoring data.
model.observable: Exact conditional complete second-public-record laws under each action; total variation between those laws after confirming identical full second public flux. Because flux matches, nonzero total variation is a finite charge-record action effect only, not an information or risk advantage.
model.uncertainty: Exact rational finite-system calculation; no stochastic independent unit, bootstrap interval or asymptotic inference

branches: predeclared equal-flux loop-toggle complete 24-site second public law
exact charge-only total-variation and one-site/replay/anti-leak controls
matrix.cost_basis_before_computation: For two first-variable bits and five second-variable bits, each joint assignment uses at most 2^(2*2+5)=512 ordered moments; 32 assignments require 16,384 moments. The baseline two assignments require 64 moments. Marginal and denominator controls keep the anticipated total under 20,000, below the prior J7L 65,536-term ceiling. This is a distinct prospective five-site contract, not a change to J7K/J7L. No next-first law is attempted.

competing_outcomes.charge_law_distinct: Both full laws normalize and share flux, but exact total variation is positive; report a finite ideal action-conditioned charge-record difference only
competing_outcomes.charge_law_equal: Both full laws normalize and total variation is exactly zero; the predeclared equal-flux action pair has no complete-second-charge contrast on this selected fixture
competing_outcomes.censored_or_invalid: Any source, action, first-mass, probability, full-record, one-site replay, term, CPU or positive-row gate fails; do not infer a charge effect or expand this contract post-data

acceptance: All ten input/source/caller hashes pass before and after; fixed first record has mass 1/4 and actions replay the J7K/J7L geometry
Exact conditional full 24-site public second law for both actions is nonnegative, normalized and retains all positive rows without a changed first record or selective outcome omission
The two public second flux arrays match; exact total variation is calculated on the entire public charge/vacuum/flux record
Each reconstructed one-site marginal replays J7K for its action and the baseline one-site two-outcome law is the established 1/2 limit; no private fields leak into public records
No next-first law, matched risk, policy emission, noisy histories, schedule arms, bootstraps or caller edits
stop_rule: Fail closed on any pin, topology/action/first-record, conditional normalization, negative mass, one-site replay, public schema, CPU, ordered-term or positive-row cap. Report a censored result if a registered resource cap fires; never increase the cap after seeing outputs.
